answer: Influence is square-rooted at the controller level: gale audits control across wallets and hosts, while river sets each controller’s voting weight to the square root of the ivory locked in one escrow. Splitting that stake among clone keys adds no weight. Matching ten independent agents with one ivory each requires 100 ivory; adding an eleventh unit of weight costs 21 more. An unrelated entrant still gets weight one with one ivory, so the rising bill tracks shared control, not network growth.
